visual.general_description: Clinical course chart combining treatment bars and arrows with a laboratory line plot over hospital days.
visual.detailed_description: The upper part of the figure shows drug rows as coloured horizontal bars and down arrows aligned to a day axis: a black arrow beside the stacked labels CBDCA, PEM and Pembrolizumab at the far left; three orange arrows beside the label mPSL 500mg; a magenta arrow beside the label Pegfilgrastim shortly after the left end; an orange bar labelled PSL1mg/kg that steps down near its right part and continues to the right edge; a pink bar labelled G-CSF; a green bar labelled Eltrombopag that begins roughly where the pink bar ends plus a gap and continues to the right edge; a blue bar labelled Cyclosporine that begins after the pink G-CSF bar has started but before the green Eltrombopag bar begins, and continues to the right edge; a purple bar labelled Caspofungin and a yellow bar labelled Meropenem spanning the same middle interval; two red arrows beside the label RCC-LR 2U; and eight green arrows beside the label PC-LR 10U. The lower part is a line plot against the day axis (ticks 1, 8, 10 and every second day to 34, then 181 after a wavy axis break) with the Admission arrow at day 8 and the Discharge arrow at day 34. A left axis reads WBC x10^2/uL (0, 23, 45, 68, 90) and a right axis reads CRP mg/dL, Hb g/dL and Plt x10^4/uL (0 to 20). WBC (dark blue) falls from a higher level to near zero just after admission and later rises to its highest level near the discharge arrow; CRP (pale yellow) rises to a sharp peak near admission and then falls to low levels; Hb (red) stays fairly flat at a mid level and rises slightly late; Plt (green) fluctuates at a low level, dips, then climbs steadily after the eltrombopag bar begins and ends near the top of the right axis at day 181.
